entries.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: one rehabilitation exercise step photograph, portrait 4:5, single pose.
Create action 124 T-AXU-002 step s01, the neutral standing starting pose for gentle supported trunk extension. The three supplied reference images ONLY fix the same adult East Asian woman's face, age, natural skin tone, black ponytail, white plain short sleeve T-shirt, charcoal dark grey long trousers, photoreal studio style, soft lighting, grey-blue seamless background. Do not copy their arm gestures.
True SIDE VIEW showing complete head, hands, hips, knees and both whole feet with generous floor margin, woman faces RIGHT. Camera at mid torso height, neutral lens perspective, full body centered. She stands comfortably with feet about hip width, BOTH entire soles and heels of simple white athletic shoes fully flat on floor. Knees softly unlocked, pelvis neutral, torso naturally upright without exaggerated chest lifting or back arch. BOTH hands lightly rest on the lateral pelvis at the iliac crests, elbows relaxed, fingers anatomically natural, no force pushing the lower back. The near hand clearly touches the near pelvic side; farther hand may be partly occluded in true profile. Head and neck in comfortable neutral alignment, calm expression looking forward. Plain grey-blue studio floor, realistic soft contact shadows.
Constraints: same reference identity, natural human limb lengths and joint connections, no chair or wall or other props; single frame only, no text, no labels, no arrows, no symbols, no watermark. Neutral starting pose must not lean backward yet. Output should be a clean anatomical teaching photo.

entries.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve
Asset type: action 126 T-AXU-004 step 01 final revised camera, one rehabilitation photograph.
Input image: edit target preserving the same woman's exact identity, outfit, supine central bent-knee position and studio scene.
Primary request: CHANGE THE CAMERA AND COMPOSITION. Camera must be positioned directly above the FOOT END on the body's CENTERLINE, looking diagonally down at 55 degrees from the floor. This is a symmetric elevated foot-end view, NOT a side view. The woman's HEAD is at TOP CENTER of the image; her TWO FEET are at BOTTOM CENTER, with her body axis vertical in the image. Her anatomical LEFT is on the VIEWER'S RIGHT, anatomical RIGHT on the viewer's LEFT. This symmetric view is essential for later left-versus-right bent-knee tilt.
Keep the same woman from the edit target: same Asian face, black ponytail lying behind her head, white short-sleeved T-shirt, dark charcoal-gray long trousers, bare feet. Same soft gray-blue studio photography, thin gray exercise mat, neutral gray floor.
Pose: lying on her back with face and chest toward the ceiling. The back of the head, both shoulder blades, upper back and pelvis stay supported on the mat. BOTH knees bent upward in the neutral middle position, close together; BOTH feet flat on mat close together with each separately visible. Both arms naturally open diagonally at about 45 degrees to the sides, resting on floor/mat, palms upward, hands relaxed. Arms are not raised.
Composition: one landscape 16:9 photograph showing ENTIRE body, both hands, both knees, both whole feet and entire mat with floor margin. The long rectangular mat is vertical from top to bottom in the image. No diagonal head-left/feet-right body alignment. Make a generous full body frame to contain opened arms. Normal human proportions; knees must not block the face or shoulders because camera is high enough.
Constraints: elevated symmetric FOOT-END view with head TOP and feet BOTTOM. Do NOT reuse the old side camera angle. Do NOT rotate only the photograph; actually reposition the camera to foot-end above the body centerline. Neutral knees centered with no left/right tilt yet. Two arms, hands, legs and feet. No crossed legs, no pillow, no shoes, no text, arrows, collage, watermark or logo.
